* The upper Riemann sum is given by:

* As the partition P gets finer, the subintervals [0, 1], [1, 2], [2, 3], and [3, 5] get smaller, and the subintervals [1, 2] and [2, 3] get smaller.

* The upper Riemann sum U(f, P) will be dominated by the terms corresponding to the subintervals [1, 2] and [2, 3], which will increase as the partition gets finer.

* The lower Riemann sum L(f, P) will be dominated by the terms corresponding to the subintervals [0, 1] and [3, 5], which will decrease as the partition gets finer.

* As the partition P gets finer, the upper and lower Riemann sums U(f, P) and L(f, P) will converge to the same value.
